title: Thousands of CAPF Officers Challenge New Law on Promotion
summary: Over 3,000 serving CAPF officers have moved the Supreme Court against the new CAPF Act, which makes it harder for cadre officers to be promoted to leadership positions. The petitioners include gallantry awardees and women officers. The law also paves the way for more IPS officers on deputation in senior roles. The Supreme Court is now dealing with a challenge to the provisions of the new act. The move comes after the officers felt they were being unfairly disadvantaged by the changes.
summary_points: Over 3,000 serving CAPF officers have moved the Supreme Court against the new CAPF Act
The petitioners include gallantry awardees and women officers
The law makes it harder for cadre officers to be promoted to leadership positions
The law also paves the way for more IPS officers on deputation in senior roles

framing.left: Left-leaning outlets framed the funding row as a national-security concern, stressing the foreign-donation angle and the demand for an audit. They highlighted the impact on the country's defense capabilities and the need for transparency in government spending.
framing.center: Centrist coverage foregrounded the challenge to the new law, emphasizing the concerns of the petitioning officers and the potential consequences for the CAPF cadre system. They noted the shift in the balance of power within the organization and the implications for promotions.

framing_hi.left: वामपंथी समाचारों ने विदेशी दान को एक राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा मुद्दे के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया, विदेशी दान के माध्यम से आय की मांग और ऑडिट की मांग पर जोर दिया।
framing_hi.center: केंद्रीय समाचारों ने नए कानून का चुनौती देने वाले अधिकारियों की चिंताओं को उजागर किया, संगठन के भीतर शक्ति के संतुलन में बदलाव और पदोन्नति के लिए इसके प्रभावों पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया।
